items.title: Karma's Gateways Open: Two Gateways, Five Ways to Give Result

items.zh: 復次，業門云何？此略有二種：一、與果門，二、損益門。與果門者，有五種應知。一、與異熟果，二、與等流果，三、與增上果，四、與現法果，五、與他增上果。
items.en: Further, what are karma's gateways? There are, briefly, two: the gateway of giving result, and the gateway of harm and benefit. The gateway of giving result comprises five kinds, it should be understood: giving a ripened result; giving a result of equal outflow; giving a dominant result; giving a result in this very life; and giving a result through another's dominant influence.

items.title: Ripened Result Tied to Destiny, and the Ten-Fold Portrait of Equal Outflow

items.zh: 與異熟果者，謂於殺生親近、修習、多修習故，於那洛迦中受異熟果。如於殺生，如是於餘不善業道亦爾。是名與異熟果。
items.en: As for giving a ripened result: by closely engaging in, practising, and repeatedly practising killing, one experiences a ripened result in the hells. As with killing, so too with every remaining unwholesome course of action. This is called giving a ripened result.

items.zh: 與等流果者，謂若從彼出，來生此間人同分中，壽量短促，資財匱乏，妻不貞良，多遭誹謗，親友乖離，聞違意聲，言不威肅，增猛利貪，增猛利瞋，增猛利癡，是名與等流果。
items.en: As for giving a result of equal outflow: upon emerging from that destiny and being reborn here as a human, one experiences a shortened lifespan; poverty and lack of resources; an unfaithful spouse; frequent, groundless slander; estrangement from friends and family; constantly hearing unwelcome words; speech that carries no real authority or credibility; and an intensified, sharpened craving, hatred, and delusion. This is called giving a result of equal outflow.

items.title: Dominant Result: How Shared Karma Shapes the Very Taste of the World

items.zh: 與增上果者，謂由親近、修習、多修習諸不善業增上力故，所感外分光澤尠少，果不充實，果多朽敗，果多變改，果多零落，果不甘美，果不恒常，果不充足，果不便宜，空無果實。當知善業，與此相違。
items.en: As for giving a dominant result: through the dominant force of closely engaging in, practising, and repeatedly practising the unwholesome courses of action, the external world one shares comes to bear little lustre; its fruit lacks substance; its fruit frequently rots; its fruit is constantly changing and unstable; its fruit frequently falls and scatters before ripening; its fruit lacks any genuine sweetness; its yield fails to endure; its yield proves insufficient; its yield turns out unfavorable; and it may bear no fruit at all. It should be understood that wholesome karma produces the exact reverse of every one of these.

items.title: Present-Life Result Opens: Eight Kinds of Resolve That Ripen Karma Early

items.zh: 與現法果者，有二因緣，善不善業與現法果：一、由欲解故；二、由事故。應知欲解復有八種。一、有顧欲解，二、無顧欲解，三、損惱欲解，四、慈悲欲解，五、憎害欲解，六、淨信欲解，七、棄恩欲解，八、知恩欲解。
items.en: As for giving a result in this very life: there are two conditions through which wholesome or unwholesome karma ripens within this present life. First, through the quality of one's resolve; second, through the significance of the object involved. Resolve, it should be understood, is of eight kinds: regard-bearing resolve, regard-free resolve, malicious resolve, compassionate resolve, hateful resolve, faithful resolve, ungrateful resolve, and grateful resolve.

items.title: Four Kinds of Resolve, Each With Its Own Classical Story

items.zh: 有顧欲解造不善業受現法果者，謂如有一，由增上欲解，顧戀其身，顧戀財物，顧戀諸有，造不善業。無顧欲解所造善業受現法果者，謂如有一，以增上欲解，不顧其身，不顧財物，不顧諸有，造作善業。
items.en: As for regard-bearing resolve producing unwholesome karma that ripens in this life: this is when someone, through a forceful resolve, clings to their own body, their own wealth, and their own possessions, and so commits an unwholesome deed. As for regard-free resolve producing wholesome karma that ripens in this life: this is when someone, through a forceful resolve, clings to none of these, and so performs a wholesome deed.

items.zh: 損惱欲解造不善業受現法果者，謂如有一，於他有情補特伽羅，以增上品損惱欲解造不善業。慈悲欲解所造善業受現法果者，謂如有一於他有情補特伽羅，以增上品慈悲欲解，造作善業。
items.en: As for malicious resolve producing unwholesome karma that ripens in this life: this is when someone, towards another being, acts with a forceful, malicious intent to harm. As for compassionate resolve producing wholesome karma that ripens in this life: this is when someone, towards another being, acts with forceful compassion.

items.title: The Remaining Four: Hatred and Faith Towards the Three Jewels, Ingratitude and the Woodcutter's Bear

items.zh: 憎害欲解造不善業受現法果者，謂如有一，於佛法僧及隨一種尊重處事，以增上品憎害欲解，造不善業。淨信欲解所造善業受現法果者，謂如有一，於佛法僧等，以增上品淨信欲解造作善業。
items.en: As for hateful resolve producing unwholesome karma that ripens in this life: this is when someone, towards the Buddha, the Dharma, the Sangha, or any similarly revered object, acts with a forceful, hateful intent to harm. As for faithful resolve producing wholesome karma that ripens in this life: this is when someone, towards the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha, acts with forceful, genuine faith.

items.zh: 棄恩欲解造不善業受現法果者，謂如有一，於父母所，及隨一種恩造之處，以增上品背恩欲解、欺誑欲解，酷暴欲解造不善業。知恩欲解所造善業受現法果者，謂如有一，於父母等，以增上品知恩欲解、報恩欲解所作善業。
items.en: As for ungrateful resolve producing unwholesome karma that ripens in this life: this is when someone, towards their own parents or any similar benefactor, acts with forceful ingratitude, deception, and cruelty. As for grateful resolve producing wholesome karma that ripens in this life: this is when someone, towards their own parents and the like, acts with forceful gratitude and genuine repayment of kindness.

items.title: The Five Acts of Immediate Retribution, Classified in Technical Detail

items.zh: 由事故者，若不善業，於五無間及彼同分中，亦有受現法果者。五無間業者，一、害母，二、害父，三、害阿羅漢，四、破僧，五、於如來所惡心出血。
items.en: As for the significance of the object: unwholesome karma, when directed at the five objects of immediate retribution or their equivalent class, likewise ripens within this present life. The five acts of immediate retribution are: killing one's mother, killing one's father, killing an arhat, causing a schism in the monastic community, and, with malicious intent, drawing a tathāgata's blood.

items.title: Equivalent-Class Offenses: Betraying Trust, Exploiting the Vulnerable, Plundering the Sacred

items.zh: 無間業同分者，謂如有一，於阿羅漢尼及於母所行穢染行，打最後有菩薩。或於天廟、衢路、市肆立殺羊法，流行不絕。或於寄託得極委重親友、同心、耆舊等所，損害欺誑。或於有苦、貧窮、困乏、無依無怙，為作歸依，施無畏已，後返加害，或復逼惱。或劫奪僧門。或破壞靈廟。
items.en: As for offenses equivalent in class to the acts of immediate retribution: this includes committing an act of sexual defilement against a fully awakened bhikṣuṇī, or against one's own mother; striking a bodhisattva in their final body before buddhahood; establishing, at a shrine, crossroads, or marketplace, a method of ritual slaughter that then spreads and continues unchecked; betraying or deceiving someone who has entrusted oneself with great responsibility — a close friend, a like-minded companion, a respected elder; taking in someone suffering, impoverished, destitute, and utterly without support, granting them refuge and safety, and then turning to harm or further oppress them; plundering the monastic community's own property; or destroying a sacred shrine.

items.title: Converting One's Own Parents, and Honouring Those Fresh From Deep Attainment

items.zh: 若諸善業由事重故受現法果者，謂如有一，母無正信，勸進開化，安置建立於具信中。如無正信，於具信中；如是犯戒，於具戒中；慳悋，於具捨中；惡慧，於具慧中亦爾。如母，父亦爾。
items.en: As for wholesome karma ripening in this life because of the significance of its object: this is when someone, whose mother lacks genuine faith, guides and enlightens her, establishing her firmly in genuine faith. Just as with faith, so too with leading a mother who violates precepts into upholding them, a stingy mother into genuine generosity, and a mother of poor judgement into genuine wisdom. As with a mother, so too with a father.

items.zh: 或於起慈定者供養承事。如於起慈定者，如是於起無諍定、滅盡定、預流果、阿羅漢果供養承事亦爾。又親於佛所供養承事。如於佛所，如是於學無學僧所亦爾。若即於此尊重事中，與上相違，由損害因緣起不善業，受現法果。
items.en: Or one may make offerings to and attend upon someone just emerging from loving-kindness concentration. As with loving-kindness concentration, so too with someone just emerging from the concentration of non-contention, the concentration of cessation, stream-entry, or arhatship. Further, one may personally make offerings to and attend upon a buddha, and, in the same way, upon the community of noble ones still training or already beyond training. Should one instead, towards these very same objects of reverence, act with harmful intent and commit an unwholesome deed, this too ripens within this present life.

blocks.text: Fascicle 9 completes the account of karmic defilement and then begins **rebirth defilement**, which is dependent origination. Today: the five ways karma gives its results, and the conditions under which karma ripens in this very life rather than a later one. Master Cháng Bǎi illustrates the eight kinds of "resolve" with classical stories, a few of which are retold below.
Karma operates through two gateways: giving results, and harm and benefit. It gives five kinds of result:

items: **Ripened** (異熟): killing practised repeatedly ripens in the hells. Venerable Miào Jìng explains the word: 異, because the cause is good or bad while the result is neutral, different in kind; 熟, because it ripens gradually.
**Equal outflow** (等流): results like the cause, in one's own body and life: a killer, reborn human, lives briefly; a frivolous speaker's words carry no weight.

**Dominant** (增上): results in one's environment. Venerable Miào Jìng: "equal outflow concerns one's own person; the dominant result concerns one's surroundings". False speech, for instance, yields a world where harvests are unreliable. Master Cháng Bǎi adds that, conversely, all food the Buddha receives is exquisitely sweet, because his wholesome deeds are complete.

blocks.text: Karma ripens in this life through two conditions: the **quality of resolve** (欲解; Venerable Miào Jìng: "a powerful wish") and the **significance of the object**.

There are eight kinds of resolve, four unwholesome and four wholesome: clinging to one's body and wealth; cruelty; hatred towards the Three Jewels; ingratitude; and their opposites. Master Cháng Bǎi's stories make them vivid:

items: **Regard for one's own body**: cattle-dealers who cut out and roasted the tongues of cows licking salt; their own tongues fell off.
**Compassion**: a eunuch who saved bulls from castration, thinking "they are about to become as I am", and at that moment regained his own manhood.
**Ingratitude**: a bear saved a lost woodcutter, who then led hunters to it for a share of the meat; when he reached for his share, his arms fell off.
**Gratitude**: Wang Xiang lay on a frozen river to catch carp for his sick stepmother.

blocks.text: Whatever one makes of the miracles, the teaching is that intensity of intention accelerates karma.

The weight of the object is clearest in the five **acts of immediate retribution** (無間業): killing one's mother, one's father, or an arhat; splitting the saṅgha; and maliciously drawing a Tathāgata's blood. Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the *Vibhāṣā*, ranks splitting the saṅgha as gravest, since it destroys the Dharma-body, the community that carries the teaching. "Drawing blood", not "killing", because a Tathāgata cannot be killed.

Offences of the same class include violating an arhat nun, striking a bodhisattva in his last life, establishing ritual slaughter at shrines, and **plundering monastic property**. Venerable Miào Jìng: "slipping it into one's own pocket is plundering the saṅgha", which is why, he says, the Buddha wanted only arhats to manage the saṅgha's property.

The wholesome side mirrors it: leading a faithless mother or father to faith, or to discipline, generosity, and wisdom; and making offerings to someone just emerging from deep meditation (loving-kindness, cessation) or just attaining stream-entry or arhatship. Venerable Miào Jìng: those two fruits because they are the entry into the noble path and its completion.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what five kinds of result does the gateway of giving result include?
options: ripened, equal-outflow, dominant, present-life, and through another's influence
quiz.why: "Giving a ripened result; giving a result of equal outflow; giving a dominant result; giving a result in this very life; and giving a result through another's dominant influence." C is fascicle 5's list, a different set. Master Cháng Bǎi: the last is like a buddha appearing — beings who make offerings dwell in peace.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain the two characters of 異熟 (ripened)?
options: 異: the cause is good or bad but the result only neutral — different in kind; 熟: it ripens only gradually
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "異 because the cause is good or evil while the result is only neutral; 熟 because it ripens little by little." Master Cháng Bǎi: the ripened result is the unobscured-neutral ālaya — different in kind from its cause, and ripened.

quiz.q: How do equal-outflow and dominant results differ, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: equal outflow is felt in one's own body and life; dominant result in one's environment
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "From context, equal outflow concerns what is felt in one's own person; the dominant result concerns one's environment." Hence it speaks of the world's lustre and fruit. Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the *Abhidharmasamuccaya*: the world shaped by beings' shared karma is the dominant result.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, by what two conditions does karma ripen in this very life?
options: through the quality of resolve, and through the significance of the object
quiz.why: "First, through the quality of one's resolve; second, through the significance of the object involved." Resolve has eight kinds; the object's weight covers the five heinous acts, their equivalents, parents, those emerging from absorption, and so on. Master Cháng Bǎi: objects are elders, the virtuous, benefactors, or the vulnerable.

quiz.q: Master Cháng Bǎi tells the story of the woodcutter and the bear, for ungrateful resolve. What happened?
options: a bear saved a lost woodcutter, who then led hunters to it for two-thirds of the meat; reaching for the meat, his arms fell off like a broken string of beads
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The woodcutter said: if you give me two-thirds of the bear when you catch it, I'll tell you where"; "when he reached with both hands for the meat, by the force of bad karma his arms fell off together like beads from a broken string." (The reading note has the hunters make the offer and the arms sliced off — logged in the correction list.)

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are the five acts of immediate retribution?
options: killing mother, father, an arhat, splitting the saṅgha, and maliciously drawing a tathāgata's blood
quiz.why: "Killing one's mother, killing one's father, killing an arhat, causing a schism in the monastic community, and, with malicious intent, drawing a tathāgata's blood." Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the *Fanyi mingyi ji*: "uninterrupted" has five senses (as in fascicle 4).

quiz.q: Citing the Vibhāṣā, Master Cháng Bǎi ranks the five. Which is gravest?
options: splitting the saṅgha is gravest, as it destroys the Dharma-body; then drawing a buddha's blood, killing an arhat, killing one's mother, and lastly one's father
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Of the five, splitting the harmonious saṅgha is gravest, since it destroys the Dharma-body; next, drawing a buddha's blood; then killing an arhat; then one's mother; lastly one's father." Splitting the Dharma-wheel saṅgha can only happen while a buddha lives. Venerable Miào Jìng: splitting the procedural saṅgha takes at least eight.
